title: A local generators and relations criterion for an inverse-image comparison
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ and $(\mathcal D,K)$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] small in a universe, with sheaves valued in a larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor for which precomposition $P_*H=H\circ P^{\mathrm{op}}$ sends sheaves of abelian groups to sheaves. Assume $\mathcal C$ has binary products and $P$ preserves them. Let $L:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ be left adjoint to $P_*$, and let $F,G$ be abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, respectively, with a morphism $\eta:F\to P_*G$. Assume the following two conditions. (i) For every $U\in\mathcal D$ and $s\in G(U)$ there is a covering family $(v_i:U_i\to U)$ and, for each $i$, an object $V_i\in\mathcal C$, a section $t_i\in F(V_i)$ and a morphism $\phi_i:U_i\to P(V_i)$ such that $G(v_i)(s)=G(\phi_i)(\eta_{V_i}(t_i))$. (ii) For every $V\in\mathcal C$, $t\in F(V)$ and $\phi:U\to P(V)$ with $G(\phi)(\eta_V(t))=0$, there is a covering family $(v_i:U_i\to U)$ and morphisms $a_i:V_i\to V$ in $\mathcal C$ and $\phi_i:U_i\to P(V_i)$ such that $F(a_i)(t)=0$ and $P(a_i)\circ\phi_i=\phi\circ v_i$. Then the morphism $LF\to G$ adjoint to $\eta$ is an isomorphism. Here $F(a)$ and $G(v)$ denote restriction maps, so their directions are contravariant.

source.place: Lines 244-284, theorem isIso_homEquiv_symm_of_locally_generated, specialized from fixed-ring module sheaves to abelian sheaves. The local hypotheses are SectionsLocallyPulledBack and RelationsLocal, lines 58-71.

proof.text:
Fix an abelian sheaf $H$ on $\mathcal D$ and a morphism $\psi:F\to P_*H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets], the underlying sets of $H$ satisfy the sheaf equalizer condition; in particular equality of sections can be checked on a covering. Suppose $G(\phi)(\eta_V(t))=0$. Apply (ii), obtaining $v_i,a_i,\phi_i$. Naturality of $\psi$ and contravariance give
$$H(v_i)H(\phi)(\psi_V(t))=H(\phi_i)H(P(a_i))(\psi_V(t))=H(\phi_i)\psi_{V_i}(F(a_i)t)=0.$$
The injective first arrow of the sheaf equalizer for this cover then implies $H(\phi)(\psi_V(t))=0$. This is a direct use of hypothesis (ii), naturality and the sheaf condition, not an additional zero-relation theorem.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.map_eq_zero, lines 89-97; underlying-set sheaf criterion: Stacks sites.tex Section 00YR, property (alpha), and Definition 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets).

proof.text:
Suppose $G(\phi_1)(\eta_{V_1}t_1)=G(\phi_2)(\eta_{V_2}t_2)$ on $U$. Put $V=V_1\times V_2$ with projections $p_1,p_2$. As $P$ preserves this product, its universal property gives $\phi:U\to P(V)$ with $P(p_j)\phi=\phi_j$. Set $t=F(p_1)t_1-F(p_2)t_2$. Naturality and additivity give $G(\phi)(\eta_Vt)=0$; step 1 gives $H(\phi)(\psi_Vt)=0$. Expanding the latter difference proves
$$H(\phi_1)(\psi_{V_1}t_1)=H(\phi_2)(\psi_{V_2}t_2).$$
Thus equal presentations give equal proposed $H$-sections, including after arbitrary restrictions. The only product used here is in $\mathcal C$ and its preserved image; no product of arbitrary objects of $\mathcal D$ is assumed.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.hasPairLifts_of_preservesLimitsOfShape, lines 69-75, and map_eq_map, lines 100-112; the product lift and subtraction are written out.

proof.text: For $s\in G(U)$ choose the cover and presentations of (i), and put $x_i=H(\phi_i)(\psi_{V_i}t_i)\in H(U_i)$. On $U_i\times_U U_j$, with projections $q_i,q_j$, the presentations $(t_i,\phi_i q_i)$ and $(t_j,\phi_j q_j)$ have the same $G$-value, namely the restriction of $s$. Step 2 therefore gives $H(q_i)x_i=H(q_j)x_j$. These fibre products exist because one is pulling back members of a covering family, by the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Apply the underlying-set sheaf equalizer of [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets] to this compatible family. It gives a unique $x\in H(U)$ restricting to every $x_i$. For the moment denote this chosen amalgamation by $h_U(s)$. This is one application of the sheaf gluing criterion to an explicitly constructed matching family.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.exists_section, lines 115-134 (compatible family and amalgamation); Stacks sites.tex Definitions 00VM/00VR, labels definition-sheaf-sets/definition-sheaf, and Section 00YR (alpha).

proof.text:
The amalgamation has a formula on every presentation, not merely on the chosen cover: if $u:T\to U$ and $G(u)s=G(\phi)(\eta_Vt)$, then
$$H(u)h_U(s)=H(\phi)(\psi_Vt). \tag{*}$$
Indeed pull back the chosen covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ to $T$, obtaining the covering $\{T\times_U U_i\to T\}$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. On each member, the restriction of the left side is the proposed value for the restricted chosen presentation; step 2 identifies it with the restriction of the right side. The injectivity in the sheaf equalizer of [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets] proves (*). If a different cover or different presentations were chosen, (*) on the original cover identifies the two amalgamations by the same injectivity. Thus $h_U$ is well defined independently of all such choices.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.exists_section, lines 135-140, and map_liftApp, lines 150-156; arbitrary-presentation formula and independence of choices.

proof.text: The maps $h_U$ are additive. Choose local presentations for $s_1,s_2\in G(U)$ on covers $\{U_i\to U\}$ and $\{W_j\to U\}$. Their common cover $\{U_i\times_U W_j\to U\}$ is covering: pull back the second cover to each $U_i$, then compose coverings, using [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. On a member $T$, write the two presentations as $(t_1,\phi_1)$ and $(t_2,\phi_2)$. With the product $V=V_1\times V_2$ and the lift $\phi:T\to P(V)$ of step 2, put $t=F(p_1)t_1+F(p_2)t_2$. Naturality gives $G(\phi)\eta_V(t)=G(\phi_1)\eta_{V_1}(t_1)+G(\phi_2)\eta_{V_2}(t_2)$. Formula (*) for these three presentations and additivity of $\psi$ show that the restrictions of $h_U(s_1+s_2)$ and $h_U(s_1)+h_U(s_2)$ agree on this cover. The sheaf equalizer of [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets] gives equality on $U$. Substituting $s_1=s_2=0$ and cancelling gives $h_U(0)=0$, so $h_U$ is a group homomorphism.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.liftApp_add, lines 159-177; scalar multiplication is unnecessary for abelian groups. Common cover supplied by Stacks site axioms 00VH.

proof.text:
For $f:T\to U$ and $s\in G(U)$, take any covering of $T$ on which $G(f)s$ has presentations $(t_i,\phi_i)$, as in (i). For a covering arrow $v_i:T_i\to T$, formula (*) applied first on $T$ with $u=v_i$ and then on $U$ with $u=fv_i$ gives
$$H(v_i)h_T(G(f)s)=H(\phi_i)\psi(t_i)=H(v_i)H(f)h_U(s).$$
The sheaf equalizer injectivity of [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets] proves $h_TG(f)=H(f)h_U$. Together with step 5, this makes $h:G\to H$ a morphism of abelian sheaves.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.liftApp_map and lift, lines 193-215; naturality follows by applying (*) twice on a presentation cover.

proof.text: Applying (*) to $s=\eta_V(t)$, $U=P(V)$, $u=\mathrm{id}_{P(V)}$ and $\phi=\mathrm{id}_{P(V)}$ gives $h_{P(V)}(\eta_Vt)=\psi_Vt$. Hence $(P_*h)\eta=\psi$. For uniqueness, suppose $b,c:G\to H$ have $(P_*b)\eta=(P_*c)\eta$. Given $s\in G(U)$, choose its presentations from (i). On each covering member, naturality gives $H(v_i)b_U(s)=H(\phi_i)b_{P(V_i)}\eta_{V_i}(t_i)$, and the same expression for $c$. These are equal by the assumed equality after $\eta$. The sheaf equalizer injectivity of [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets] gives $b_U(s)=c_U(s)$. Thus for every $H$, $b\mapsto(P_*b)\eta$ is bijective from $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(F,P_*H)$.

source.place: LocallyGenerated.lift_fac and hom_ext, lines 225-242; existence and uniqueness of the extension, computed on sections.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:LF\to G$ be adjoint to $\eta$, and write $A_H:\operatorname{Hom}(LF,H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F,P_*H)$ for the given adjunction. Naturality in $H$ says $A_H(b\alpha)=(P_*b)\eta$. By step 7 and bijectivity of $A_H$, precomposition with $\alpha$ is bijective for every $H$. Explicitly, taking $H=LF$ supplies $\beta:G\to LF$ with $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{LF}$. For $H=G$, injectivity of precomposition with $\alpha$ and the identity $(\alpha\beta)\alpha=\alpha(\beta\alpha)=\alpha=\mathrm{id}_G\alpha$ imply $\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}_G$. These two identities exhibit $\beta$ as the inverse of $\alpha$. This last argument uses only the natural hom-bijection defining the assumed adjunction and category identities; it does not invoke a separate Yoneda theorem.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_homEquiv_symm_of_abelian_local_generators_relations {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] (J : Precoverage C) (K : Precoverage D) (_hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (_hK : K.IsSiteForCoverings) (P : C ⥤ D) [HasBinaryProducts C] [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) P] (hP : ∀ H : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD w}, Presheaf.IsSheaf J.toGrothendieck (P.op ⋙ H.obj)) (L : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD w} ⥤ Sheaf K.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD w}) (adj : L ⊣ Sheaf.precompositionOfSheafPreservation P hP) (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD w}) (G : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD w}) (η : F ⟶ (Sheaf.precompositionOfSheafPreservation P hP).obj G) (_hgen : ∀ (U : D) (s : G.obj.obj (op U)), ∃ (I : Type (max uD vD)) (U' : I → D) (v : ∀ i, U' i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows U' v ∈ K U ∧ ∀ i, ∃ (V : C) (t : F.obj.obj (op V)) (φ : U' i ⟶ P.obj V), G.obj.map (v i).op s = G.obj.map φ.op (η.hom.app (op V) t)) (_hrel : ∀ (V : C) (t : F.obj.obj (op V)) (U : D) (φ : U ⟶ P.obj V), G.obj.map φ.op (η.hom.app (op V) t) = 0 → ∃ (I : Type (max uD vD)) (U' : I → D) (v : ∀ i, U' i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows U' v ∈ K U ∧ ∀ i, ∃ (V' : C) (a : V' ⟶ V) (φ' : U' i ⟶ P.obj V'), F.obj.map a.op t = 0 ∧ φ' ≫ P.map a = v i ≫ φ) : IsIso ((adj.homEquiv F G).symm η)
